narrative.overview:
The native interface is a funeral ledger set in warm bone on blue-black ink. Large, sharp words give names and numbers ceremony; small ruled entries keep the game readable. The spirit realm supplies movement and depth behind the ledger. This records the incumbent Flutter world and its branding extension, rather than a replacement identity.

The product premise comes from [README](../README.md), [gameplay](../docs/gameplay.md) and [architecture](../docs/architecture.md). Visual authority is [Veil](lib/theme/veil.dart), the [ledger kit](lib/widgets/ledger.dart), and the implemented [threshold](lib/screens/threshold_screen.dart) and [arrival](lib/brand/splash_gate.dart). Values in the frontmatter translate Flutter logical pixels to portable `px`; the Dart source remains the implementation authority.
keyCharacteristics: Warm bone words and fine rules on tinted ink.
Fraunces for names and large numerals; DM Sans for instructions, labels and figures.
A reaper's single light carries the interface's active colour.
Spacious ceremonial entry, with compact ledger controls inside the game.

rules.name: The Borrowed Light Rule
rules.body: Active interface colour comes from the player's reaper; new screens use the theme's primary colour rather than inventing an accent.

rules.name: The Name and Number Rule
rules.body: Names and ceremonial numerals use `Veil.display`; instructions and ledger figures use their respective `Veil` helpers.

dos: Do reuse `Veil`, the ledger kit and `ReapersMark` on new native screens.
Do let short screens scroll, scale the wordmark down and wrap action details.
Do keep launch motion finite, honour reduced motion and expose startup recovery.
Do rebuild and relaunch after changing installed native artwork.
donts: Don't treat the provisional logo default as a final user selection.
Don't add decorative eyebrows to arrival; its mark, name and premise already establish the hierarchy.
Don't expose the underlying game to interaction or accessibility focus while the arrival gate covers it.
Don't infer Android or tablet visual approval from a successful compile or the iOS correction verdict.
